name: Stone cake
summary: Also bánh Lơ khoải. A long cake of rice, corn, and sticky rice, yellow or purple, of the Dao and the Nùng. It is left in the stream for months until moss grows, then scraped, and cut in strips about as wide as a finger.
origin: The high communes of Đồng Văn, on Dân Việt. It appears at Dao áo dài festivals and Tết.
howToEat: Dân Việt gives three ways, and all stay: in place of noodles, as a cool bite, or boiled until soft with palm sugar and roasted peanuts.
A 2026 civil date for the festival is Check on arrival.
where: The high communes of Đồng Văn.
seoTitle: Stone cake in Dong Van — banh da, banh Lo khoai
seoDescription: Bánh đá, also bánh Lơ khoải, is stream-soaked until moss grows, then eaten in place of noodles, cool, or boiled with palm sugar and peanuts.
